name: input.keyboard.key_down
description: Press a virtual key by name and leave it held indefinitely. Returns immediately. Pair with `input.keyboard.key_up` (or rely on connection-close cleanup) to lift. Use this for multi-verb chord workflows (Shift+drag, Ctrl across multiple invocations); for single-verb timed holds use `input.keyboard.key {duration_ms}`. Per issue #70.

vk.description: Key name. Same vocabulary as `input.keyboard.key` (e.g. `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `F4`, `a`). Case-insensitive.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`. The agent records the key as held on this connection; see lifecycle §2.8 for cleanup semantics.

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SendInput` with INPUT_KEYBOARD + `KEYEVENTF_KEYDOWN` (the default — no flag for plain down). No matching up event; the key stays held until `input.keyboard.key_up` or connection close.

x-implementations.name: keybd_event
x-implementations.description: Win32 `keybd_event` legacy fallback for NT 4 / 9x where SendInput is unavailable.

windows-modern.description: SendInput with KEYEVENTF_KEYDOWN. Agent registers the vk in the per-connection held-input set so lifecycle §2.8 can release it on connection close. Same RawInput / DirectInput limitation as input.keyboard.key — apps reading via GetAsyncKeyState against the kernel keyboard table will not see the held state. Targets that respect user32's keyboard-state aggregation (most apps including modern frameworks) WILL see the key as held during subsequent verbs (e.g. Shift held during a click registers as Shift+click). UIPI applies same as input.keyboard.key.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+; keybd_event on NT 4 / 9x. Same per-connection held-input tracking as modern. No UIPI on classic.
